text:
samir: Heads up — during the long-context perf runs this morning I saw a sharp KV eviction spike and hit-rate drop around 10:12 UTC. eviction counter went from ~200/min to ~2.5k/min for a few minutes. Logs show a pile of 'kv_fragment_miss' entries. Anyone else see this?

casey: Yep I saw the same in the nightly rollup. p99 latency rose a bit too. Suspect fragmentation + our new kernel scheduling patch interacting with large sequence lengths.

maria: Do we have a Prometheus view for residency + eviction rate per model/shard? I only saw global rates which hide hot shards.

casey: No per-shard dashboard yet. Quick PromQL I used to triage: 
```
sum by (model, shard) (rate(kv_evictions_total[5m]))
sum by (model, shard) (kv_residency_bytes)
sum by (model, shard) (kv_hits_total) / sum by (model, shard) (kv_requests_total)
```
That highlighted model=wizard-13b, shard=3 as the hotspot.

elliot: FWIW I pushed kernel change KERNEL-2029 last week that touched hash placement for KV keys. Could be that the distribution skewed for long sequential prefixes.

samir: Good catch. If the hash skewed, we'd see increased frag reuse drop and more evictions. Can we add seq-length buckets to the metrics (e.g., short/medium/long) so dashboards can filter by request context length?

maria: We can approximate buckets at ingest time without too much overhead. Proposal: add label `seq_bucket` with values "<2k", "2k-8k", ">8k" on sample metrics and make residency a gauge sampled at 1s on active shards. Downside: cardinality increase — we should only enable for flagged models.

casey: Agreed. For observability I also want:
- eviction_rate{model,shard,seq_bucket} (5m rate)
- residency_bytes{model,shard} (gauge)
- frag_reuse_ratio{model,shard} = kv_fragment_reused_total / kv_fragment_allocated_total
And a panel that cross-plots seq_bucket vs eviction_rate.

samir: Can someone draft the Grafana panel and a Prometheus recording rule? It's getting noisy in alerts.

maria: I'll add recording rules to staging: 
```
- record: job:kvcache:evictions:rate5m
  expr: sum by (job, model, shard, seq_bucket)(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m]))
- record: job:kvcache:residency_bytes
  expr: sum by (job, model, shard)(kv_residency_bytes)
```
I'll scope seq_bucket to models in `observability_flag=true` to limit cardinality.

runtime-bot: [alert] kvcache:eviction_rate_high firing (group: infra/kvcache). trigger: job:kvcache:evictions:rate5m > 1000 for 3m. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-evictions

deploy-bot: Noted — KERNEL-2029 rollback is scheduled to canary next hour unless we decide to patch.

casey: For repro, run the long-context load with KV profiling enabled: 
```
# local repro (use perf cluster)
python tools/perf/kvcache_repro.py --model wizard-13b --seq-len 12k --duration 10m --enable-profiling --tag seq_bucket=>8k
```
It will emit flamegraphs and a small trace showing fragment allocations. Path: tools/perf/out/<ts>/*.svg

elliot: If repro shows shard 3 has >60% of new fragment allocations, that's consistent with hash skew. Fix options: re-hash function, add shard-balancer, or increase eviction threshold for long-context. Re-hash might cause mass-migration so prefer shard-balancer first.

maria: Also recommend changing eviction alert to use a signal for "sustained" vs "burst" — alert only if rate > threshold and frag_reuse_ratio < 0.6. That avoids noisy bursts during planned heavy loads.

samir: Action items:
- casey: create Grafana panels + add the recording rules PR (staging only) — can you do today?
- maria: implement seq_bucket label gating and new recording rules, limit to observability_flag models.
- elliot: prepare a shard-balancer design doc and simulate re-hash impact.
- runtime-bot: keep alert muted for the canary window and post updates.

casey: Yep will open PR 1) grafana panel json 2) prometheus recording rules, and attach a sample dashboard screenshot.

maria: I'll push the seq_bucket change behind a feature flag and run the repro on perf cluster. Will post flamegraph link when done.

samir: Thanks. If anyone hits this again before the fixes, add `?seq_bucket` param to the repro and drop a trace here. :thumbsup:
